data.result:
Overall: The route and tower provide a usable geographic through-line, but signal readability, screen direction, and dust treatment need attention before review. Still frames cannot establish gait speed, cadence, foot sliding, rider bounce, or whether the gallop feels realistic/full-pace; those require playback.

Urgent blockers
• Shot 2: The left-moving horse has very little lead room and is close to exiting frame. Reframe or adjust timing so the full silhouette remains readable.
• Shot 3: Both the tower signal and rider response are too small to read clearly. The raised-arm gesture is visible only as a silhouette, while the flag looks static and no signaling action/person is apparent. Use a closer insert, stronger pose, or clearer signal change.
• Directional continuity: Shot 1 approaches camera/front-left, Shot 2 travels left, Shot 3 travels away, and Shot 4 travels rightward toward the tower. Without a visible turn or neutral bridge, this may read as an axis/screen-direction reversal rather than one continuous run.
• Dust continuity/realism: Shot 2 has strong visibility, but its large, soft-edged cloud resembles a fog bank more than localized hoof dust. In Shots 1, 3, and 4 the dust is weaker and often blends into the tan road. Match density, origin, scale, and persistence across cuts while retaining contrast against the green meadow.

Shot-specific framing/visibility
• Shot 1: Horse and rider are readable, but the clipped fence at upper left is distracting. Dust is faint and low-contrast.
• Shot 2: Best horse profile and dust contrast, but cramped on the leading edge. The dark rider loses some detail against the horse/hedge.
• Shot 3: Strong central route-to-tower composition, but action is undersized. The cropped red building at far right is an unnecessary edge distraction.
• Shot 4: Tower destination is clear, but horse/rider are very small and the dust plume is cropped at the lower-left/bottom edge. Excess empty meadow reduces departure-action emphasis.

Acceptable rough-cut scenery limitations
• Low-poly trees, hedges, fences, tower, flat lighting, uniform grass, and the overly clean road are understandable free-asset/previs limitations.
• These become blockers only if this cut is expected to demonstrate final photorealism; otherwise prioritize action readability, dust behavior, and continuity first.
